title: bqmm — Adversarial code review & empirical validation
text: ALD density & quantile: dald integrates 1 τ-quantile mu τ tested; R density Stan asym_laplace_lpdf agree machine precision. Kozumi–Kobayashi RNG σ-scaling: single-σ factoring correct (v = σ·w substitution absorbs √σ). Empirically, rald reproduces ALD quantile closed-form variance (ratio 0.998) scales σ². lme4 → Stan sd_map: “coefficient varies fastest within level” assumption correct, verified structurally (intercept vs slope columns identified directly t(Zt)) across random-slope, 3-coefficient, unbalanced, crossed, repeated-factor, single-observation-group interaction designs — 100% columns mapped right variance component. Parameter recovery (correct ALD multilevel DGP, 100 reps, n=200): bias(β₀)=−0.04, bias(β₁)=+0.02, mean σ̂=0.998 (true 1.0), mean σ_u=0.739 (true 0.7). Essentially unbiased. Koenker sandwich (compute_ywh_sandwich): n-scaling correct (variance ∝ 1/n, ratio 8.2 8× n change — decisively old 1/n²), one-coef closed form exact, agrees quantreg’s nid sandwich fixed effects (0.0061/0.0067 vs 0.0067/0.0065). Simulation-based calibration (tools/sbc.R, 300 sims, diagonal model): rank histograms β₀, β₁, σ sd_re consistent uniform (χ² GOF p = 0.39 / 0.52 / 0.84 / 0.34; mean ranks ≈ 128 = L/2). evidence miscalibration — posterior computed correctly end--end (formula → Stan data → sampling → extraction).

title: Valid inference under the asymmetric Laplace likelihood
text: asymmetric Laplace distribution (ALD) convenient working likelihood quantile regression: mode--quantile check-loss connection make Bayesian computation straightforward (Yu Moyeed, 2001). misspecified almost real data-generating process, misspecified likelihood produces posterior whose spread wrong asymptotic variance quantile-regression estimator. Naive credible intervals posterior correct frequentist coverage.

title: Valid inference under the asymmetric Laplace likelihood
text: Yang, Wang (2016) restore validity multiplicative sandwich re-uses posterior covariance “bread”: Vadj=ΣpostGΣpost, V_\text{adj} = \Sigma_\text{post}\, G\, \Sigma_\text{post}, Σpost\Sigma_\text{post} posterior covariance fixed effects GG meat — variance asymmetric-Laplace working-likelihood score. score si=σ−1xi(τ−𝟏{ri<0})s_i = \sigma^{-1} x_i\,(\tau - \mathbf{1}\{r_i<0\}) conditional residuals rir_i, meat G=σ−2∑g(∑∈gxiψi)(⋅)′G = \sigma^{-2}\sum_g\big(\sum_{\g} x_i\psi_i\big)\big(\cdot\big)' (cluster-robust grouping factor; default), independence analogue. Using Σpost\Sigma_\text{post} bread makes correct mixed model: posterior covariance already encodes multilevel pooling, adjustment keeps random-effect contribution fixed-effect uncertainty fixing misspecified ALD scale. correct specification G≈Σpost−1G \approx \Sigma_\text{post}^{-1} correction reduces ≈Σpost\approx \Sigma_\text{post}.

title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: regression met models mean outcome: “average, one-unit change x moves y β.” often wrong summary. Three situations recur practice. spread changes. growth, income, biomarker data variability outcome grows predictor. mean model reports one slope; reality 90th percentile rises far faster 10th. tails point. Clinicians care patients high end risk marker, average patient; ecologists care minimum river flow, mean flow. questions quantiles. effect distributional. treatment may shift everyone equally — may compress bottom distribution leaving top alone. Quantile regression (Koenker 2005) answers directly. Instead mean, models chosen conditional quantile — median (τ = 0.5), 10th percentile (τ = 0.1), 90th (τ = 0.9), whole grid . coefficient β(τ) read : “one-unit change x moves τ-th percentile y β(τ).” Sweeping τ 0 1 traces predictor reshapes entire conditional distribution, just center.

title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: Real data rarely single exchangeable sample. Patients nested hospitals; measurements repeated within subjects; students crossed schools neighbourhoods. Ignoring structure understates uncertainty discards information. Multilevel (mixed-effects) models add random effects — cluster-specific deviations drawn common distribution — cluster borrows strength others keeping signature.

title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: Bayesian treatment delivers full posterior uncertainty every quantity (fixed effects, variance components, predictions), handles hierarchical shrinkage coherently, lets encode prior knowledge. also comes one subtlety specific quantile regression — likelihood working approximation — Section 6 treats carefully. bqmm built default settings handle subtlety .

title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: Write τ-th conditional quantile outcome observation cluster j linear predictor fixed random parts: Qτ(yij∣xij,uj)=xij⊤β(τ)+zij⊤uj. Q_\tau(y_{ij} \mid x_{ij}, u_j) \;=\; x_{ij}^\top \beta(\tau) \;+\; z_{ij}^\top u_j . β(τ) fixed effects quantile τ (shared across clusters) u_j random effects cluster j, drawn mean-zero normal, u_j ~ N(0, Σ). design vectors x z built formula — bqmm write y ~ x + (1 + x | g) exactly lme4. estimation trick. Classical quantile regression minimises check loss ρ_τ(u) = u(τ − 1{u < 0}). obvious likelihood Bayesian — notice minimising check loss equivalent maximising likelihood asymmetric Laplace distribution (ALD) (Yu Moyeed 2001). bqmm uses ALD working likelihood: yij∣⋅∼ALD(μij,σ,τ),μij=xij⊤β+zij⊤uj, y_{ij} \mid \cdot \;\sim\; \mathrm{ALD}\big(\mu_{ij},\, \sigma,\, \tau\big), \qquad \mu_{ij} = x_{ij}^\top\beta + z_{ij}^\top u_j , scale σ > 0. mode/τ-quantile density sits exactly linear predictor, fitting recovers quantile regression estimate. Priors complete model: weakly-informative normals β, half-normals σ random-effect SDs, (correlated random effects) LKJ prior correlation matrix. bqmm scales defaults data rarely need touch . Key idea. ALD device, belief errors. makes quantile estimate computable Bayesian framework. Section 6 explains one place matters — uncertainty — bqmm corrects .

title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: important section. ALD working likelihood, naive Bayesian posterior covariance fixed effects correct sampling variance quantile-regression estimator — credible intervals built can badly - -cover (Yang et al. 2016). known, well-understood issue, bqmm corrects default. correction follows Yang et al. (2016): replace naive posterior covariance sandwich re-uses posterior covariance “bread” score-variance “meat”, Vadj=ΣpostGΣpost, V_{\mathrm{adj}} \;=\; \Sigma_{\text{post}}\; G\; \Sigma_{\text{post}}, G variance ALD working-likelihood score. Using posterior covariance bread makes valid multilevel models: Σ_post already carries random-effect contribution fixed-effect uncertainty, correction keeps fixing misspecified scale. correct specification correction collapses ≈ Σ_post, . simulation across homoscedastic heteroscedastic two-level designs, adjusted intervals cover just nominal 95%, whereas naive intervals -cover slopes; see vignette("bqmm-inference") package’s review report. take-away practice: Report adjusted = TRUE intervals unless specific reason . package’s reason exist generic ALD fit. title: A Primer on Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: posterior trust worse posterior. Always check: Sampler convergence. bqmm surfaces warnings automatically — split-R̂ 1.01, low effective sample size, divergent transitions. Treat stop sign. usual fixes: Raising adapt_delta toward 0.99 increasing iter cures divergences low-ESS warnings; variance correlation parameters slowest mix benefit . Inspect posterior bayesplot ecosystems: Posterior predictive checks. fitted model generate data look like ? Overlay replicated datasets observed outcome: Posterior predictive check: observed outcome density (dark) draws fitted model (light). Systematic mismatch flags misfit quantile interest may capture. Non-crossing. fitting several τ, confirm fitted quantiles monotone (enforce noncrossing = "rearrange").
code: fit <- bqmm(distance ~ age + (1 | Subject), Orthodont, tau = 0.5,             chains = 4, iter = 4000,             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12)) library(posterior) summarise_draws(as_draws(fit))            # R-hat, ESS per parameter  library(bayesplot) mcmc_trace(as_draws(fit), regex_pars = "b_") yrep <- posterior_predict(fit)            # draws x observations bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay(Orthodont$distance, yrep[1:50, ])

text: Clusters, just observations. Random-effect variances correlations need many groups (rule thumb: ≥ 20–30) estimable. handful large clusters enough. Extreme quantiles need data. τ = 0.05 0.95 estimated sparse tail; expect wider intervals harder sampling. Raise adapt_delta. Scale predictors. Centring scaling continuous predictors improves sampling geometry makes priors easier set. Diagonal vs unstructured. Start cov = "diagonal". Move "unstructured" one grouping factor, enough clusters, substantive reason expect correlated random effects. cores > 1 parallelises chains; systems package must default library path parallel workers find . cores = 1 always works. Report quantile(s) modelled, adjusted intervals, random-effect SDs (correlations), convergence diagnostics.

title: Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: Familiar lme4 formula interface — y ~ x + (1 + x | group); nested crossed random effects work box. One many quantiles single call (scalar vector tau). Valid inference — Yang, Wang & (2016) posterior-variance correction applied default, fixing well-known invalidity naive asymmetric-Laplace credible intervals. Verified simulation cover nominal level. Correlated random effects — cov = "unstructured" adds LKJ-correlated random intercept slope, correlation reported VarCorr(). Non-crossing — optional post-hoc rearrangement fitted quantiles never cross. Ecosystem citizen — works posterior bayesplot stacks via as_draws(), ships usual lme4/rstanarm-style methods.

title: Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression
text: Primer — thorough, accessible guide applied researchers: method, fitting, priors, inference, diagnostics, visualization. Get started — short tour. Multilevel structure — random intercepts/slopes, correlated crossed effects. Valid inference — naive intervals fail correction works. Review & testing report — validation evidence behind package. Function reference.

title: Yang-Wang-He multiplicative variance correction — compute_ywh_multiplicative
text: Computes V = Sigma_post %*% G %*% Sigma_post, mixed-model form YWH correction (see ywh_adjust()). ALD working-likelihood score observation s_i = (1/sigma) x_i (tau - 1{resid_i < 0}), meat G = (1/sigma^2) sum_i x_i x_i' psi_i^2 (independence) G = (1/sigma^2) sum_g (sum_{g} x_i psi_i)(...)' (cluster-robust), psi_i = tau - 1{resid_i < 0}.

title: bqmm 0.1.0
text: First release. bqmm() — Bayesian mixed-effects quantile regression via asymmetric Laplace likelihood Stan, lme4-style formula interface (y ~ x + (1 + x | group)) supporting nested crossed random effects. cov = "diagonal" (default) cov = "unstructured" — latter adds LKJ-correlated random effects single grouping factor; VarCorr() reports posterior-median correlation matrix. Fitting one several quantiles single call (vector tau). Post-hoc non-crossing rearrangement fitted quantiles (Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val Galichon, 2010). Yang, Wang (2016) posterior-variance correction valid frequentist inference, exposed vcov(object, adjusted = TRUE). lme4/rstanarm-style S3 methods integration posterior bayesplot ecosystems.
